hints.title: Preserving Unassigned Attributes
hints.text: In three-valued relational logic, comparing a column to a constant evaluates to unknown when that column holds no reference value.

hints.title: Disjunctive Null Predicate
hints.text: To select customers not referred by account number two, include both referee_id <> 2 and referee_id is null in your filter condition.

hints.title: Query Formulation Blueprint
hints.text: Select name from Customer where referee_id <> 2 or referee_id is null.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT name
FROM Customer
WHERE referee_id != 2 OR referee_id IS NULL;
```

complexity.notes: Single table scan evaluating three-valued logic predicate.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: WHERE referee_id != 2 silently omits rows where referee_id is null because NULL != 2 evaluates to UNKNOWN.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Linear scan with index support on referee_id identifies qualifying customers without memory allocation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Mastery of three-valued SQL logic where NULL requires IS NULL or coalesce guards.

solutions.approach: Three-Valued Logic Filter with Is Null

solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def find_customer_referee(customer: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    filtered = customer[(customer['referee_id'] != 2) | (customer['referee_id'].isna())]
    return filtered[['name']]
